A National Weather Service storm survey team, in |coordination with Suffolk County Fire Rescue and Emergency |Services has confirmed an EF0 tornado in the Mattituck area of|Suffolk County NY.||Based on analysis of the storm survey findings and OKX dual pol |radar reflectivity, velocity and derived data (including a |tornadic debris signature), it was determined that an EF0 tornado|first touched down at Juniper Hill farms around 1117 pm, damaging|a greenhouse and downing a couple of large trees on the property.||The tornadic circulation likely lifted or skipped along as it|tracked east northeast across a one mile stretch of remote wooded|area, before touching down and shearing several tree tops and|large limbs in the vicinity of Cottage Way, Walnut Place, and |Lipco Road, between Sound Avenue and Old Sound Avenue. Peripheral |straight line wind damage to a large tree was noted near Shirley |Road and Horton Avenue to the north of Sound Avenue as well.||The tornadic circulation likely skipped east northeast in the|vicinity of Old Sound Avenue/Main Street over Love Lane and|Wickham Avenue with spotty tree damage noted, before definitively|touching down once again between Wickham Ave and Mary's Road to |the north of Pike Street, with a large maple tree sheared a few |feet from its base, minor siding and roof damage, and leaf |splatter on the west and south sides of homes. This most |prominent damage path, about 50 to 75 yards in width, continued |across Mary's Road, where 3 evergreen trees were snapped at their |base in a convergent pattern (the 2 southernmost trees laying in a|northeast direction and the northernmost tree laying in a |southeast direction). The tornado continued eastward across the |Mattituck-Cutchogue Jr/Sr high school track, twisting and damaging|a large scoreboard, overturning metals benches, and laying down a|100 ft section of wind fence on the north side of the adjacent |tennis courts in a northerly direction (again consistent with a |convergent wind pattern). The tornado then continued east over the|high school, ripping up large sections of asphalt roofing |material over one of the main buildings. The damage across the |high school grounds was the most severe along the path, consistent|with tornadic winds of 75 to 85 mph.||The tornado then exited east over an area of homes on Village |Lane, causing significant tree and fence damage to several homes, |before likely lifting around 1120 pm as the rotating storm |continued eastward over the farm fields and vineyards that lay to|the east. No visible damage was noted to the east of this point, |marking the presumed end of the tornado path.

Widespread 6+ inch snow reports came in across the county. Trained spotters reports included 6.7 inches from Monroe, 6.4 inches in Walden, 8.1 inches from Highland Mills, and 7.0 inches in Newburgh. Cocorahs reports included 8.5 inches in Port Jervis and 6.5 inches in Warwick. General public reports included 7.5 inches in Chester and Pine Bush, 7.0 inches in New Windsor, and 6.3 inches in Cornwall-on-Hudson.
Heavy snow was reported across the county. Snowfall reports included 6.5 inches at 2W Putnam Valley, 6.0 inches from Cold Spring, and 5.0 inches from COOP at Carmel Hamlet.

Heavy snow fell across the northern half of the county. A Cocorahs report had 6.5 inches in Katonah, a COOP report came in with 6.0 inches in Shrub Oak, a trained spotter reported 6.0 inches in White Plains, and public reports of 6.0 inches at 2 NE Somers and 5.7 inches at Croton-on-Hudson.

Heavy snow fell across the county into the morning rush hour. Snowfall reports of 6.1 inches in Stony Point via Cocorahs, 5.9 inches 1.7 SSW Spring Valley via Cocorahs, and 5.7 inches at 0.6 SE New Hempstead via Cocorahs. Also a trained spotter reported 5.6 inches at 1 WSW New City.  Most of these reports came in likely after some compaction of the snow took place as temperatures were marginal and right near freezing.

Heavy snow fell across the northern half of the county. Snowfall reports from trained spotters of 6.8 inches at 1 E Danbury, and 6.3 inches in New Fairfield were reported.  Also a Cocorahs observer reported 6.2 inches at 2.4 NNE Ridgefield.

Heavy snow fell across much of the southern half of the county, especially further west. A trained spotter 6.4 inches in Weston, and 6.0 inches in Fairfield, and a Cocorahs observer reported 6.1 inches in Norwalk, with a public report of 6.0 inches at 4 SSE Easton and 5.5 inches at 2 SW Bridgeport.

Heavy snow fell across the northern half of the county into the morning commute. A public report from 4 ENE Naugatuck of 6.2 inches was reported. A trained spotter from North Haven reported 5.5 inches. Cocorahs observers reported 5.5 inches in Hamden and 5.5 inches in Meriden.  The following snowfall reports came in just after sunrise as temperatures were marginal which likely led to some compaction just before the measurements were taken.

Heavy snow was reported across the northern half of the county into the morning commute. A trained spotter reported 6.1 inches in Cromwell, and a Cocorahs observer reported 5.0 inches in Higganum. Some compaction likely took place with these reports as they came in well after the steadier snow ended as temperatures were marginal and close to freezing and then rose above freezing.

Heavy snow fell across the county into the morning commute. Cocorahs observer reported 6.7 inches in Norwich, and 5.5 inches at 5.2 SE Norwich.  A public observer reported 5.5 inches at 3 WSW Franklin.

Heavy snow fell across the western portion of the county and carried into the morning commute. The public reported 6.0 inches in Bloomingdale at a time in which compaction likely had not yet set in. Cocorahs reported 5.5 inches almost 2 hours later in Wayne.

Heavy snow fell into the morning commute across Western portions of Bergen County. Cocorahs reported 6.0 inches in Oakland, and the public reported 6.0 inches in Allendale at times after some compaction would have started as temperatures began to climb above freezing within an hour or two after sunrise and the steadier snow had ended.  A trained spotter reported 5.1 inches in Ramsey in the late morning which likely was measured after compaction occurred.

Wet snow fell across the eastern half of the county. Snowfall amounts ranged generally from 3 to 5 inches across this portion of the county. A Cocorahs observer reported 4.8 inches from Little Falls and 4.6 inches from Hawthorne, while a public report of 3.6 inches was reported from Totowa after likely compaction.

A general 2 to 5 inches fell across the eastern portion of the county. Cocorahs reports of 5.0 inches at 1.8 ESE Montvale, 3.6 inches in Tenafly and 2.7 inches in Palisades Park were observed. A trained spotter reported 4.8 inches in River Vale and 3.8 inches at 1 NNE Begenfield.

The majority of snow reports ranged from 4 to 5 inches across the southern portion of the county. A trained spotter reported 5.3 inches in Hartsdale, 5.0 inches in Peekskill, and 4.5 inches in Yonkers. Public reports included 5.0 inches in Armonk, 4.8 inches at 1 WSW New Rochelle, with a Cocorahs report of 5.3 inches from Armonk. Thus, just short of reaching warning criteria.

A trained spotter reported 4.5 inches of snow in Milford. Cocorahs observers reported 3. 8 inches in Madison  A COOP observer reported 4.0 inches in Guilford and 3.8 inches at 2.7 WSW Guilford Center, with broadcast media reporting 4.5 inches in New Haven.
A trained spotter reported 3.3 inches in Westbrook. A Cocorahs observer reported 4.0 inches nearby, near the northern edge of the zone in Killingworth.
Cocorahs observers reported 4.0 inches in Groton, 3.0 inches in Niantic, 3.0 inches in Old Lyme, and 4.3 inches in Mystic. A trained spotter reported 3. 4 inches at 1 NNE Groton.
Cocorahs observers reported 3.5 inches in Manhasset Hills, Herricks, and at 0.2 SSE Albertson which is at the southern border of zone.  The public reported 5.1 inches in Glen Cove.

Trained spotters reported 5.0 inches in Centereach, 5.0 inches in Smithtown, 4.5 inches in Farmingville, along with a COOP observer reporting 4.2 inches in Mt. Sinai. An NWS Employee reported 4.2 inches in Stony Brook, and Broadcast Media reported 3.5 inches in South Huntington.

A trained spotter reported 4.5 inches in Mattituck, along with a COOP observer reporting 4.5 inches in Orient Point. An NWS employee reported 3.8 inches in Sound Beach, along with a NWS Office report of 4.4 inches in Brookhaven Labs / Upton.
An NWS employee reported 1.8 inches in Bay Shore and a trained spotter reported 2.0 inches in Ronkonkoma. Islip airport reported 2.7 inches of snow.
A COOP observer reported 4.4 inches in Bridgehampton along with a public report 4.5 inches in Shirley.

A Cocorahs observer reported 3.5 inches at 0.2 SSE Albertson along the northern edge of the zone, and 1.0 inches in Wantagh. A trained spotter reported 2.1 inches further north in New Hyde Park.  Mainly 1 to 2 inches fell across Southern Nassau as temperatures were mainly just above freezing.

A general 1 to 3 inches fell across Manhattan on non cement surfaces as temperatures will mainly a degree or so above freezing. Central Park reported 1. 8 inches of snow, and a Cocorahs observer reported 3.0 inches at 1 WNW Fordham.

A general 2 to 3 inches of snow was reported across the zone. LaGuardia reported 2.3 inches of snow, and a public report of 3.2 inches in Whitestone. A Cocorahs report came in at 2.5 inches at 0.3 SE Little Neck.
A general 1 to 2 inches of snow fell across much of the zone. Kennedy airport reported 1.5 inches of snow, while Howard Beach reported 2.0 inches of snow from a Cocorahs report.
Light accumulations of 1 to 2 inches of snow fell across Brooklyn. Broadcast media reported 1.4 inches of snow at 1 SSW Flatbush.
A general 3 to 5 inches fell across the zone. A Cocorahs report of 5.0 inches was submitted for Montclair and 4.8 inches in Verona. A public report of 4.1 inches was submitted for 1 W Cedar Grove.
A general 2 to 4 inches fell across the zone. Newark Airport reported 1.7 inches of snow, with the western edge of the zone receiving 3.7 inches via a trained spotter in Bloomfield.

A general 1 to 3 inches of snow fell across the zone.  A trained spotter reported 2.4 inches in Plainfield. A Cocorahs report from Clark which is right along the eastern border of the zone reported 3.0 inches of snow and 1.0 inches of snow at 0.8 WSW Westfield, and 1.5 inches at New Providence.
A light snowfall around 1 inch fell across the zone.  A cocorahs report of 1.0 inches was reported at 0.6 NNW Cranford.
A general 1 to 3 inches fell across the zone. A COOP observer reported 2.5 inches in Harrison, a Cocorahs observer reported 2.0 inches in Kearny, and a trained spotter reported 1.2 inches in Hoboken.

Not many reports came in for this county / zone, but the few reports received included a public report of 5.6 inches at 1 NE Fordham and 4.5 inches in Yonkers just above the northern border of the zone. Amounts in the zone fell below warning criteria. it appears amounts were on the order of 4 to 5 inches.

Snowfall totals averaged over 6.0 inches across the county, although amounts varied greatly with some western locations generally receiving less being on the outer edge of the precipitation shield when colder air arrived. Trained spotters reported 15.5 inches at 1 WNW Monroe and 6.1 inches at Salisbury Mills. Public reports included 9.4 inches in Chester and 6.5 inches at 2 SW Greenwood Lake. Cocorahs reports included 8.5 inches in Port Jervis, but only 2.2 inches in Walden.

The northern half of the zone had snowfall totals at or exceeding 6 inches of heavy wet snow. A trained spotter reported 7.0 inches in Peekskill, with a public report of 6.3 inches at 3 ESE Peekskill. The public also reported 7.1 inches at 1 N North Castle. A report of 4.0 inches came in early the following morning at Shrub Oak 0f 4.0 inches but this was after hours of compaction.

Very heavy wet snow fell across Putnam County resulting in a impactful heavy wet snow into the morning commute. Broadcast media reported 11.9 inches at 3 N Putnam Valley. A Public report came in with 12.0 inches at 1 WSW Lake Carmel. Fire Department and Rescue reported 17.0 inches at 4 NNE Fahnestock State Park.  Cocorahs reported 10.5 inches in Cold Spring and Amateur radio reported 6.4 inches in Mahopac. A trained spotter also reported 13 inches in Kent via social media. Accumulations appeared to be greatly impacted by elevation.

Not many reports were received from Rockland County overall. The public reported 2.0 inches at 1 NNW Chestnut Ridge, with Cocorahs reports at lower elevations closer to the Hudson reported 1.4 inches at 0.6 SE Hempstead and 1.1 inches at Stony Point. Higher elevations likely had noticeably more snow based on the behavior of this storm and radar returns observed but we did not receive the reports from higher elevations.

A cocorahs observer reported 3.5 inches in Armonk. A 1 to 4 inch snowfall was observed across the northern portions of Southern Westchester, with amounts closer to an inch across far southern portions of the zone and mainly on colder surfaces as temperatures were mainly above freezing as this was an elevation based snowfall event across the Lower Hudson Valley.

Reported snowfall varied greatly along the western edge of Northern Fairfield. Most of the zone received snowfall under 6 inches going east and south.  The higher elevations reported over 6 inches of snow along the far western portions of the zone as temperatures were marginal and snow reports were strongly based on elevation. A trained spotter reported 7.5 inches at 4 WNW Fairfield. Broadcast media reported 7.0 inches at 3 NW Ridgefield at a higher elevation. The remaining reports all came in well below 6 inches. Cocorahs reports included 2.7 inches in Redding, 2.0 inches in Shelton, 1.9 inches in Bethel and 1.5 inches in New Canaan and Sandy Hook.

Cocorahs reports came with 3.4 inches in Naugatuck and 2.7 inches at 1.2 WSW Seymour. Broadcast media reported 3.8 inches at 4 ENE Naugatuck, with the public reporteding 3.3 inches in Southbury and a public reported of 7.0 inches at 1 NNW Oxford.  Reports along the southern eastern portion of the zone at lower elevations were under 3 inches.

Law enforcement reported that the first victim, a 16-year-old girl, was pulled out of the water off the intersection of Beach 108th Street and Shore Front Parkway. Simultaneously, police reported first responders got the second victim, a man in his late teens or early 20s, who drowned in the waters off Beach 98th Street ��� ten blocks to the east of the first fatal drowning. Both victims were rushed to St. John���s Episcopal Hospital, where they died, police sources said. The two victims were among five people pulled out of the waters off Rockaway Beach on the same day, the other three distressed victims survived.

Kitburi was already unconscious when he was pulled from the water shortly after 7:30 p.m. by three nearby surfers, according to the East Hampton Town Police. An EF0 tornado touched down three times along a mile and a half path in Newburgh, NY. The tornado developed around 615 pm and moved east-southeast from the 400 block of South Plank Road to Park Avenue between 2nd and 3rd Streets. The tornado brought down multiple large branches and a few large trees. It also caused a wall to collapse at Rick's Automotive on South Plank Road, causing the roof to collapse. The damage was consistent with an EF0 tornado on the Enhanced Fujita Scale, with winds from 65 to 85 MPH.

Snowfall totals varied across Orange County from west to east.  Cocorahs observers reported of 13.1 inches in Port Jervis and 10.3 inches in Warwick. A trained spotter reported 11.7 inches in Walden.  The public reporte 10.2 inches in Newburgh, 10.2 inches in Pine Bush, and 9.5 inches in Florida. A trained spotter reported 9.2 inches in Salisbury Mills.||Snowfall totals averaged over 6.0 inches across the county, although amounts varied greatly with some western locations generally receiving less being on the outer edge of the precipitation shield when colder air arrived. Trained spotters reported 15.5 inches at 1 WNW Monroe and 6.1 inches at Salisbury Mills. Public reports included 9.4 inches in Chester and 6.5 inches at 2 SW Greenwood Lake. Cocorahs reports included 8.5 inches in Port Jervis, but only 2.2 inches in Walden.
Heavy snow was reported via Cocorahs observers with 6.5 inches reported in Cold Spring and 6.0 inches in Nelsonville. A report of 5.6 inches was submitted via Broadcast Media from Putnam Valley.

Snow amounts varied greatly across Northern Fairfield with Trained spotters reporting 8.5 inches in New Fairfield, 8.0 inches at 4 SSE Sherman, and 4.4 inches at Danbury. However, amounts were noticeably lower going south with Redding reporting 4.0 inches, Stamford reporting 3.5 inches, Norwalk reporting 3.0 inches, and a Cocorahs report of 2.6 inches in Brookfield. Well more than half the zone reported snow that fell short of warning criteria with some amounts on the order of 1 to 3 inches along the immediate sound shore with Bridgeport NWS observation of 3 .0 inches.

An accumulating snow fell across Northern New Haven County with 5 inch totals reported at 1 N Cheshire and Middlebury by the public, and 4.6 inches in Waterbury and 4.0 inches in Hamden from Cocorahs. Amounts further south ranged from under an inch along the Sound shore, to most 1 to 3 inches across the southern part of Northern New Haven County.

An accumulating snow took place across northern portions of Middlesex County, with a mix and change to rain. Trained spotters reported 6.5 inches in Cromwell and 3.9 inches at 3 WNW Cromwell.  Cocorahs reported 3.2 inches in Durham, 3.0 inches in Middlefield, and 1.9 inches in Higganum. Amounts decreased sharply from here going south and southeast. Amounts averaged well below warning criteria across Northern Middlesex County.

Accumulating snow took place across the zone, with amounts that were reported between 3 and 5 inches. Cocorahs reports were 4.5 inches in Wayne, 4.3 inches in West Milfored, 4.1 inches in Little Falls, and a trained spotter came in also with 3.8 inches in Wayne. These amounts fell short of warning criteria with the snow going over to mixed precipitation.

An accumulating snow took place before a mix and change to rain. Reports averaged in the 2 to 4.5 inch range for the most part. Cocorahs reported 4.0 inches in Verona and 3.5 inches at 1.3 NE West Caldwell.  There was a public report of 4.4 inches in North Caldwell and 3.5 inches in West Orange. Amounts fell short of warning criteria.

An accumulating snow took place before a change to a wintry mix. Trained spotters reported 6.2 inches at 2 NNE Franklin Lakes, 5.7 inches at 1 N Franklin Lakes, 4.0 inches at Franklin Lakes, 4.0 inches at Glen Rock, and 4.0 inches at 1 ESE Westwood, and 3.4 inches in Fair Lawn. A Cocorahs observer reported 5.5 inches at Oakland.  Amounts fell off quickly heading southeast. Amounts averaged below warning criteria across the zone.

An accumulating snow occurred across Rockland County before a mix and changeover to a wintery mix and rain. Amounts averaged between 3 and 4 inches across much of the zone and fell short of warning criteria. Cocorahs reported 4.1 inches at 1.7 SSW Spring Valley, 4.0 inches in Stony Point, and 3.6 inches at 0.6 SE New Hempstead. A Trained spotter reported 3.0 inches in New City. The public reported 3.0 inches at 2 W Buchanan.

An accumulating snow took place across Northern Westchester. Amounts ranged mostly between 3 and 5 inches. Trained spotters reported 4.6 inches in Peekskill, and 4.0 inches at 1 SE Croton-on-Hudson. Cocorahs reported 4.0 inches in Shrub Oak. Amounts were less going south and east with a quicker mix and changeover to rain. Amounts fell short of warning criteria.

Two brothers went into the water in a red flagged area at Coney Island Beach on Thursday 7/27 in Brooklyn. The beach had signs saying Danger Drowning Risk from Rip Currents, and no lifeguards were on duty in that area. Good samaritans rescued one boy, but the other was not found. His body washed up on Saturday 7/29.

Snowfall totals included; 7.0 inches at 1 E Commack via broadcast media, 7.0 inches at 1 WSW Smithtown via the public, 7.0 inches in Stony Brook via an NWS employee, and 6.6 inches in Huntington via the public.

A wet snow accumulated across Southern Nassau County, with amounts averaging under warning criteria. Amounts were right around 4 to 5 inches across northern sections of the zone, with amounts closer to 3 inches across the immediate south shore. Some totals included: 5.3 inches at 1 SSW South Massapequa via Cocorahs, 5.2 inches in East Meadow via an NWS Employee, 5.0 inches in Floral Park and at 1 SE Bethpage via the public, along with 4.6 inches at 1 ESE Malverne via Cocorahs.

A wet snow fell across Southwestern Suffolk County, with the snow initially in the form of a wintry mix. Amounts were higher across the northern portion of the zone, and lower closer to the shore. Amounts on average ranged from 2 to 4 inches, with some places closer to 4 to 5 inches across northern portions of the zone. Snow amounts ranged from 3.3 inches in Bay Shore via an NWS Employee, to 2.8 inches in Sayville via Cocorahs, and 4.3 inches at MacArthur Airport (Islip).

A wet snowfall accumulated across Southeastern Suffolk County. The snow initially began as rain and a wintry mix. Snow accumulated mainly between 2 and 5 inches, with average snow amounts falling below warning criteria. Some snow amounts were as follows; 3.5 inches in Mastic and 5.0 inches in Hampton Bays via Emergency Management.

A wet snow accumulated across Northeastern Suffolk County which initially began as a wintry mix.  Snow amounts averaged below warning criteria across the zone with a few reports right along the north shore at warning criteria. Some snowfall reports were as follows; 4.0 inches in Calverton and Riverhead, 3.6 inches at 1 W Jamesport via the public, 3.7 inches at 3 WNW Aquebogue, 5.5 inches in Upton via the NWS, and 6.5 inches at 2 NNW Ridge via a trained spotter.

A wet snow accumulated across the Bronx, with the county falling just below warning criteria. The public reported 5.0 inches at 1 NNE East Tremont, and broadcast media reported 4.6 inches at 1 SSW Parkchester. Just to the north in Yonkers 6 inches was reported.

A wet accumulating snowfall occurred in Northern Queens. The snow initially began as a wintry mix. Snowfall totals fell short of warning criteria. LaGuardia Airport reported 3.3 inches, while 1 W Whitestone reported 5.2 inches.

A wet snow accumulated across Southern Queens after initially being a wintry mix.  Snowfall amounts ranged from 5.7 inches in Howard Beach from a trained spotter, to 4.2 inches at Kennedy Airport, to 3.3 inches at 1 S Elmhurst. Most totals ranged from 2 to 5 inches across the zone.

A wet snow accumulated across Brooklyn after initially beginning as a wintry mix. Most amounts ranged from 2 to 4 inches. Snow totals included; 3.0 inches in Midwood via a trained spotter, and other 2 to 4 inch reports.

A wet snow accumulation took place in Staten Island, with amounts mostly ranging from 2 to 4 inches.  Westerleigh reported 3.3 inches via the public and 1.5 inches at 2 ENE Annadale via the public a couple of hours before the snow tapered off.
A wet snow accumulated after initially beginning as a wintry mix with mainly under 4 inches across Manhattan. Snow totals included 3.2 inches via the Central Park Conservancy.

A very heavy wet snowfall occurred across Northern Fairfield County. Reports from trained spotters included; 13.2 inches at 2 NNW Bethel, 11.5 inches at 4 SSE Sherman, 11.4 inches at 4 NNE Bethel, and 9.7 inches at 5 ENE Redding.

A heavy wet accumulating snow occurred across Southern Fairfield County. Snowfall totals from trained spotters included; 6.2 inches at 2 N Stamford, 6.0 inches at 1 SE Norwalk, 9.2 inches at New Canaan, 7.4 inches at Weston, and 6.5 inches at 3 NNE Stamford.  Bridgeport Airport reported 7.6 inches.

Heavy wet snow fell across Northern New Haven with the public reporting 12.5 inches in Waterbury, and trained spotters reporting 11.0 inches in Middlebury, 9.1 inches in Hamden, with Amateur radio reporting 10.0 inches in Wallingford.
Heavy wet snow fell across Southern New Haven County. Trained spotters reported 8.6 inches in Madison and 8.0 inches in New Haven. Amateur radio reported 9.0 inches in Milford.
Heavy wet snow fell across Northern Middlesex County. A trained spotter reported 11.5 inches in Cromwell. Amateur radio also reported 10.0 inches in Durham and 7.0 inches at 1 NNW Killingworth.

Heavy wet snow fell across Southern Middlesex, especially away from the immediate coast. A trained spotter over in Madison on the border of Southern New Haven and Southern Middlesex reported 8.6 inches. Running just along the northern edge of the zone 2.7 WNW Chester Center reported 7.5 inches via Cocorahs, and 1 NNW Killingworth reported 7.0 inches, thus half the zone estimated to have reached warning criteria on a line oriented WSW to ENE running just away from the shoreline.
Heavy wet snow fell across Northern New London County. A trained spotter reported 7.5 inches in Norwich and 6.0 inches at 2 SSE Ledyard Center.

Wet snow accumulated across Southern New London County, but warning criteria snow was met in consistent fashion just north of the northern boundary of the zone.  There was one report of 6.0 inches at 1 NNE New London, but it was the only report of 6 inches. Stonington only reported 1.2 inches as of 0900. Other coastal locations in New London County like East Lyme, Old Lyme, and Mystic which all reporting under 2 inches by mid morning did not report again.
Heavy wet snow accumulated across Western Passaic County. A trained spotter at 1 NE West Milford reported 9.5 inches.
Heavy wet snow fell across Eastern Passaic County. A trained spotter reported 9.5 inches in Clifton and the public reported 8.5 inches in Totowa.
The public reported 9.1 inches in Franklin Lakes, 8.0 inches in Mahwah, and 7.0 inches at 1 W Fair Lawn.
Heavy wet snow fell across Eastern Bergen County. A trained spotter reported 9.8 inches in River Vale, 8.3 inches at 1  ESE Westwood, and 8.1 inches in Bergenfield, and 6.5 inches in Lyndhurst.
Heavy wet snow fell across Western Essex County. The public reported 9.5 inches at Essex Fells, 8.0 inches at 1 SSW West Orange, and 7.0 inches in Livingston.

Wet snow accumulated across Eastern Essex County. No six inch snow amounts were reported. Newark Airport reported 4.9 inches and nearby Maplewood via Cocorahs reported 3.7 inches just before the snow tapered off.

Heavy wet snow fell across Western Union County with amounts increasing further west across the zone. The public reported 7.5 inches in Mountainside, 5.7 inches in Plainfield after some compaction, and a trained spotter reported 7.9 inches in New Providence.

Wet snow accumulated across Eastern Union County but amounts were below warning criteria. A trained spotter reported 5.0 inches in Rahway, the NWS observation at Newark reported 4.9 inches, and amateur radio reported 4.0 inches at Linden.

Wet snow accumulated across Hudson County, with amounts falling below warning criteria. Trained spotters reported 5.0 inches at 2 NE Newark, 3.9 inches in Kearney, and 3.7 inches in Hoboken. A CO-OP Observer in Harrison reported 5.5 inches.

A narrow band of heavy snow got into Richmond County (Staten Island) with the highest amounts over the southern half of the zone. A Cocorahs observer reported 7.8 inches at 1 N Tottenville. The public reported 10.0 inches at 1 WSW Tottenville, 9.5 inches at 1 SE Huguenot, 9.1 inches at 1 SSW Huguenot, 8.6 inches at 1 E New Dorp, 7.8 inches at 1 N Tottenville, and 6.8 inches at Westerleigh.  Further north in the zone only 3.5 inches was reported at 1 WNW Tompkinsville which corresponded well to radar and the band orientation.

A band of heavy snow got into most of Brooklyn, with perhaps far northern parts of the zone averaging below warning criteria with less reports further north and based on radar analysis and location of the stronger radar reflectivity. However most of the zone reported with warning criteria snowfall. Snowfall reports from Broadcast Media included 7.3 inches at Midwood. A trained spotter reported 8.0 inches at Sheepshead Bay and 5.2 inches at 2 WNW Crown Heights. Public reports around Bay Ridge varied from around 5 to 7.6 inches, and 6.5 inches in Williamsburg. The lowest report was from 2 W Crown Heights at 4.7 inches. Thus amounts of those reported averaged more than warning criteria and more than half the zone spatially reached warning criteria.

A narrow band of heavy snow got into Western Union County, with the highest amounts over the southern half of the zone. Trained spotters reported 7.3 inches in Plainfield and and a Cocorahs observer reported 7.7 inches at 1 ENE Clark. There was also a report from the public of 5.8 inches at Clark which at close to the mid point of north and south. Lower amounts were reported further north, with 4.4 inches reported at Kenilworth in the afternoon likely after some compaction of the snow.

The northern edge of a narrow band of heavy snow got into Eastern Union County. The zone appeared to average below warning criteria with a report from Newark via NWS official observation of 4.2 inches. A trained spotter reported 5.5 inches in Elizabeth. Reports just to the east across the river into Hudson County ranged from 3 to 4 inches. These reports go in line with higher amounts south and lower amounts north. It appears that 4 to 5 inches was the norm across Eastern Union County, falling just short of warning criteria.

The far northern edge of a band of accumulating snow got into Western Essex County with a general 2 to 4 inches reported from north to south. A trained spotter reported 2.0 inches further north into West Caldwell, while the general public reported 3.0 inches in West Orange, and 4.0 inches further south into Millburn.

The northern edge of a narrow band of moderate to heavy snow got into Eastern Essex County. An official NWS Observation from Newark Airport yielded 4.2 inches of snow, with surrounding observations just outside the zone yielding general amounts of 2 to 4 inches. Amounts fell below warning criteria across the zone.

The far northern edge of a narrow band of moderate to heavy snow got into Hudson County with the highest amounts over the southern half of the zone based on reports and radar reflectivity returns. A general 3 to 5 inches of snow fell across the zone as amounts fell below warning criteria. A CO-OP observer reported 4.0 inches in Harrison, a trained spotter reported 3.1 inches in Hoboken, a Cocorahs observer reported 3.0 inches in Kearny, and the public reported 5.5 inches further south in Bayonne.

The far northern edge of a band of moderate to heavy snow stationed itself just south of Manhattan, although radar reflectivity returns indicate that the band scraped far southern Manhattan although reports from far Southern Manhattan did not come in. There were 5 and 6 inch reports just to the ESE over Kings (Brooklyn) and over Hudson County in NE NJ. The NWS Official Observation for the NWS indicated 2.0 inches in Central Park, and 3.2 inches at 1 SE Greenwich Village (Madison Park) via an NWS Employee / Contractor.

A general 2 to 3 inches fell across Southern Westchester with more significant snow associated with a heavy band falling to the south of the zone. A trained spotter reported 3.0 inches a 2 ESE Scarsdale, and a Cocorahs observer reported 2.7 inches in Armonk. Public reports also came in from 2.1 to 3.4 inches of snow.

A band of heavy snow got into the far southern portion of Queens County. However, most of the zone fell short of warning criteria from a coverage perspective. This is based on reports and radar reflectivity returns. The highest amount reported was from the general public in Breezy Point with 8.9 inches and this matched up with radar returns as Breezy Point sticks out as the most southern point. Broadcast media at 4 ENE Breezy Point (Coney Island vicinity) reported 8.0 inches. Also, the NWS Official Observation at JFK reported 6.2 inches. However, this was only a very narrow stripe of warning level snow across far southern portions of the zone.  A trained spotter reported 3.3 inches a 2 S Elmhurst, the public reported 3.0 inches at 1WNW Elmhurs, and the Official NWS Observation at LGA reported 3.3 inches of snow.  There was also a 3.3 inch amount reported just to the west across Northern Brooklyn.

A band of heavy snow got into the far southern portion of Nassau County. The zone was on the far northern edge of the moderate to heavy snow band. However, most of the zone fell short of warning criteria from a coverage perspective. This is based on reports and radar reflectivity returns. Trained spotters reported 5.0 inches in Island Park to the south, and 2.7 inches in Syosset to the north. An NWS employee reported 3.0 inches in East Meadow up towards the northern part of the zone. Broadcast media reported 5.0 inches in Rockville Centre, with the general public reporting 6.0 inches in Bellmore. A public report from Bethpage came in at 3.0 inches and 3.1 inches in Manhasset Hills.  Most places received 3 to 5 inches of snow north of the Southern State, with amounts closer to 5 and 6 inches right along the immediate south shore towards the beaches.

A band of heavy to moderate snow moved just to the immediate south of Northern Queens. Amounts ranged around 3 inches across the zone. The Official NWS Observation from LGA reported 3.3 inches. A public report at 1 WNW Elmhurst came in at 3.0 inches.  Also a report came in from Woodside at 3.0 inches.

The northern edge of a band of moderate to heavy snow barely missed Northern Nassau with mainly a light accumulating snow across the zone. Amounts ranged from most 2 to 4 inches across Northern Nassau. The public reported 3.1 inches in East Williston, 3.0 inches in Glen Cove, and 3.4 inches in Plainview.

A heavy to moderate band of snow scraped southern portion of Southwest Suffolk. In general 3 to 5 inches fell across the zone. Trained spotters reported 4.0 inches in Copiague, 4.5 inches in West Islip, and 3.6 inches at 1 WNW Babylon. Broadcast media reported 4.9 inches in Babylon.  The airport at Islip reported 3.4 inches.

A band of heavy snow just missed Northwest Suffolk to the southwest. An accumulating snowfall occurred with mainly 3 to 4 inch snow amounts. NWS Employees reported 3.0 inches in Centereach and 2.0 inches at 1 NE South Huntington. The public reported 3.1 inches in Commack, 3.0 inches at 1 WSW Smithtown, 1 SSW Nesconsett, and 3.0 inches in Setauket.

Reports of around 2 inches came in for the Bronx with the band of heavy snow going just to the south. A cocorahs report of 2.0 inches came in at 1 NE Riverdale and a public report of 2.1 inches at 1 ENE East Tremont.

A general 2 to 4 inches fell across Northeastern Suffolk County as the moderate to heavy band of snow missed just to the southwest.  A Cocorahs observer reported 2.8 inches in Riverhead, and the public reported 3.4 inches in Mount Sinai.  In Upton the Official NWS Observation came in at 3.0 inches.

A general 2 to 5 inches of snow fell across Southeastern Suffolk County. A band of heavy snow just missed Southeastern Suffolk to the south and west. A portion of the band barely scraped far southwestern parts of the zone. The public reported 5.3 inches in Shirley, 4.5 inches in Mastic Beach, 3.1 inches in East Hampton, and 3.8 inches in Blue Point.

Shortly after 6 p.m. after lifeguards had left for the day, Christian Perkins, who had just turned 17 the week before, and 16-year-old Elyjha Chandler, went into the ocean near Bay 2 in Riis Park, to cool off during the heatwave. The boys did not know how to swim. Witnesses say the teens tried to jump up when a large wave came, but the wave consumed them, and they never resurfaced. By 6:35 p.m., 911 calls were made to report the missing boys. The call resulted in a massive rescue response that included FDNY Marine Units and divers, NYPD Harbor Units, NYPD Harbor Base Divers, and Coast Guard and water teams from Sandy Hook, Cape Cod and Atlantic City. They searched for the boys until darkness fell on Friday, with no sight of them. They resumed the search the next day, until the search was suspended on Saturday night. Coast Guard crews had searched a total of more than 600 square miles. The search area extended from Sandy Hook, New Jersey, to Long Beach, New York, and offshore approximately 20 nautical miles. ||Their bodies were found over a week later. Police said one of the bodies was found Saturday night June 29 around 9 p.m. near Beach 114th Street and Ocean Promenade in Queens. The other body was found Sunday June 30th around 10:45 a.m. near Beach 149th Street and Rockaway Beach Boulevard��� almost two miles west.

Aisha Mohammed, 18, and Zainab Mohammed, 17, of the Bronx were reported missing around 8:10 p.m. Friday near Stillwell Avenue in Brooklyn by a bystander who said they entered the water and disappeared from view. The teens were found on the shoreline at 9:15 p.m. and rushed to Coney Island Hospital, where they were pronounced dead according to the NYPD. ||A relative said it was only their second time going to the beach. They were hanging out with a group of about 12 other people enjoying a sunny day at the popular beach when the skies suddenly opened up in a heavy downpour. A family member said he was returning to the group when he spotted the girls being swept out to sea in a strong current.

On August 11th at about noon, a Suffolk County Park Ranger who was patrolling Smith Point was on the outer beach between cut 1 and cut 2 was was notified that a person was in distress in the water. Fire Rescue officials were also notified and activated the Mastic Beach FD, along with the local Marine Incident Response Team (MIRT), which in addition to Mastic Beach FD also consists of Mastic Fire Department, Eastport FD, Center Moriches FD, and East Moriches FD. Also activated were the Mastic and Mastic Beach Ambulance Companies. ||The Mastic FD Marine Incident Response Boat 5-12-26 was already out conducting overwatch for the Suffolk County USAR team that was conducting a drill on the Forge river when the call went out. With a full crew and an EMT on board, they broke off from the drill immediately once the call went out for persons in the water on the ocean side at Smith Point.||Mastic Beach FD, under command of Chief Luis Grego and Assistant Chief Jason Sharp, also sent members to the dock to meet the boat. The remaining members of the MIRT team also began to quickly muster crews and resources for response. Suffolk Police Marine Rescue Boat Marine Mike was also dispatched. While units were responding from Police and Fire Departments, the Park Ranger and a good Samaritan had attempted to send out a life ring, but the man was unresponsive. ||Suffolk County Ocean Rescue lifeguards responded to the location, which is outside of the protected zone of jet skis and located the unresponsive 70-year-old male. He was taken to shore where CPR was initiated. Smith Point EMTs were on scene and assisted with care, which was turned over to members of the Mastic Beach Ambulance.||Park Rangers met with Suffolk Police at the outer beach entrance where police requested that the road to the outer beach be closed at the booth. Mastic Beach Ambulance transported the male to Long Island Community Hospital where he was later pronounced dead.

The Nissequogue River dam broke due to the flash flooding causing the entire Blydenburgh Pond to empty into the river. The river overflowed its banks, sending water into homes and nearby streets. Two residents were trapped in their homes and had to be rescued.
Long Island Expressway is closed between Exit 52 and 51 westbound due to flooding. NY State called to assist with pumping water.

Trained spotters reported 3.2 inches at 4 NNW New Fairfield, 2.5 inches at 1 E Danbury, and 2.4 inches at 3 WSW Shelton.  Cocorahs observers also reported 3.0 inches at Ridgefield, 2.8 inches 4.5 SSE Bethel, and 2.5 inches in Monroe.

Public observers reported 4.5 inches in Wolcott and 2.9 inches at 2 SE Beacon Falls. Cocorahs observers reported 3.5 inches in Naugatuck and 2.5 inches in Waterbury. A trained spotter reported 3.3 inches in Seymour.

An emergency manager reported 5.5 inches in Lisbon and a Cocorahs observer reported 2.2 inches in Norwich. A few hundred power outages were reported across interior New London from weighted wet snow and wind. More power outages were reported just north of the CWA border, this information was passed along to us by DESPP / DEMHS.

Trained spotters reported 4.0 inches at 4 NNW New Fairfield and 2.7 inches at 2 ESE Danbury.  Cocorahs observers reported 3.0 inches at Bethel and 2.7 inches at Brookfield. Light freezing rain amounts were also reported.

Cocorahs observers reported 3.0 inches at Naugatuck, 2.0 inches in Meriden, and 1.8 inches in Hamden. Light amounts of freezing rain (0.02 inches) was also detected by the Meriden ASOS, and 0.03 inches at the New Haven ASOS.
A cocorahs observer reported 3.9 inches in Port Jervis, with trained spotters reporting 3.7 inches at 2 S Montgomery Airport and 2.5 inches at Monroe.
Cocorahs observers reported 4.5 inches at 0.3 S Nelsonville and 3.5 inches at Cold Spring.
A cocorahs observer reported 3.5 inches in Shrub Oak and 2.5 inches at 2.8 NNE Peeksill, and a public observer reported 3.0 inches in Somers.

A trained spotter reported 10.0 inches of wet snow at 1 WNW Monroe, while cocorahs observers reported 12.8 inches in Port Jervis, 8.2 inches at 4 SSE Chester, and 7.2 inches in Warwick. There was a public report of 4.1 inches at 2 SSW Stewart Airport. From Broadcast Media (News 12 Hudson Valley) the following impacts were reported: Parts of the area saw several inches of thick, slushy snow during the overnight hours into the morning commute. And while the precipitation is much needed after months without rain, the sudden conditions downed utility lines and trees; caused outages and, according to state police, dozens of accidents. Also, Slick roads and high winds remain a concern and utility officials say, as of late afternoon, there were more than 4,000 customers without power. In Warwick, a transformer fire on Newport Bridge Road left dozens in that neighborhood without power. I-84 westbound was shut down during the morning commute from exits 15 to 4 due to multiple disabled tractor-trailers and motor vehicle accidents, according to state police, with the roadway opened by late morning.
A cocorahs observer reported 4.5 inches in Cold Spring.
The public reported 7.5 inches at 5 N West Milford and a cocorahs observer reported 3.4 inches in West Milford.
The NY Department of Highways reported a downed tree on NY 27 eastbound in the area of Spring Close Highway in East Hampton at 127 PM Local Standard Time.
NY Department of Highways reported a downed tree on Northern State Parkway eastbound at exit 42S, in Dix Hills, NY at 152 PM EST. All lanes were open, but the exit ramp was blocked.
The public reported a large tree down on an SUV on Beverly Road in Lake Grove, NY at 1030 PM Local Standard Time.
A measured high wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at a mesonet station located in Stony Brook, NY (measurement taken at 159 feet above ground) at 614 PM Local Standard Time.
The Department of Highways reported a downed tree at 147 PM Local Standard Time on Long Island Expressway/I-495 in westbound at Exit 34 in North Hills, NY with 1 right lane of 4 lanes closed.

Trained Spotters reported 8.5 inches in Washingtonville, 7.0 inches in Monroe, New Windsor, and Salisbury Mills.  Cocorahs reports included 8.3 inches at 4 SSE Chester, 7.1 inches in Warwick, 6.8 inches at Cornwall-on-Hudson, and 6.2 inches at Port Jervis.

A trained spotter reported 6.5 inches at 3 WNW Fahnestock State Park. Cocorahs reported 6.3 inches at 0.3 S Nelsonville, and 6.0 inches at Cold Spring early the following morning, with a report of 5.6 inches via Newspaper / Media at Putnam Valley.

A Cocorahs observer reported 4.5 inches at 2.8 NNE Peekskill and 3.6 inches at Armonk early the following morning. During the evening higher totals of 5.5 inches were reported at Croton-on-Hudson and Ossining via the public. Also during the evening a public report of 6.0 inches was received from 1 SE Croton-on-Hudson (the only one at 6 inches). A Cooperative observer reported 4.3 at Shrub Oak. Thus the far northern portions of the county did have a few reports close to 6 inches, but the zone easily averaged below warning criteria.

Trained Spotters reported 5.2 inches in Monsey, 5.0 inches in New City, and 3.8 inches in Nyack.  Cocorahs reported 5.5 inches at 1.7 SSW Spring Valley, 4.4 inches at 1 NW Stony Point, with the Fire Dept reporting 6.5 inches in Congers. Only one report reached 6 inches, all other reports were below 6 inches with the average across the county / zone at advisory level.

Trained spotters reported 3.1 inches in Yonkers and 1.2 inches in Pelham, with amateur radio reporting 1.5 inches at 1 N Port Chester as amounts were much lower closer to Long Island Sound. The public reported 3.5 inches at 1 NNW Tuckahoe, 3.4 inches in Larchmont, 3.0 inches at Eastchester, and 3.0 inches at 1 SSE Greenville as most snowfall totals reached advisory level.

NWS Employees reported 3.2 inches in Stony Brook, 3.2 inches in Centereach, and 2.8 inches in Mt. Sinai. A Cooperative observer reported 3.6 inches in Centerport, with the public reporting 3.1 inches at 1 NNE Greenlawn, and 3.1 inches at 1 SSW Port Jefferson. Most of the zone, especially further north reached advisory criteria.

Trained spotters reported 4.0 inches in Syosset, 2.5 inches in Levittown, with the public reporting 3.9 inches at East Williston, 3.9 inches at 1 W Plainview, and 3.8 inches at 1 ENE Glen Cove. A Cocorahs observer reported 2.7 inches in Manhasset Hills.

NWS Employees reported 2.5 inches at 1 E East Meadown, 2.4 inches in East Meadow, with Cocorahs observers reporting 2.3 inches in Massapequa and 2.1 inches in Bellmore. The public reported 3.0 inches in Massapequa, 3.2 and 3.0 inches in Plainview, and 3.0 inches in Farmingdale. Most of the zone averaged below advisory criteria.

Trained spotters reported 5.5 inches of snow at 4 NNW New Fairfield, 5.2 inches in New Fairfield, 4.3 inches in Danbury, and 3.8 inches in Weston.  Cocorahs reported 4.5 inches in Bethel, 4.3 inches at 2.4 NNE Ridgefield and 4.0 inches in Brookfield.  Snow reports were at advisory level criteria.

An official NWS observation from Bridgeport Airport reported 2.5 inches of snow. Cocorahs reported 3.0 inches in Stratford, 3.0 inches in Shelton, 3.0 inches at 2.6 SSE Trumbull, and 2.5 inches at Monroe, with the public reporting 2.3 inches in Greenwich, and 2.1 inches at 1 S Darien.  Snow reports reached or just fell short of advisory level criteria across the zone.

Amateur Radio reported 3.0 inches in Durham and 4.5 inches in Middletown.  Cocorahs reported 3.5 inches at 1.4 W Middlefield and 3.0 inches at Higganum. Snowfall totals averaged at advisory level criteria across the zone.

Cocorahs observers reported 3.3 inches in Hamden, 3.3 inches in Meriden, and 2.3 W Southbury with 3.5 inches. Amateur radio reported 5.0 inches in Wallingford.  Much of zone reported advisory level criteria snowfall.

A trained spotter reported 4.0 inches in North Haven, with a Cooperative observer reporting 3.0 inches in Guilford, and Cocorahs reporting 2.2 inches at 2.7 WSW Guilford Center, and 1.8 inches at 1.3 N Madison Center.  Northern portions of the zone reached advisory level criteria, with southern portions of the zone falling short of advisory level criteria.

The public reported 4.0 inches at 3 SW Lebanon, and 3.7 inches at 2 WNW Gales Ferry. Cocorahs reported 2.0 inches at Norwich.  Norther portions of the zone reached advisory level criteria, while locations further south in the zone received less and were short of advisory level criteria.

An Official NWS Observation from LaGuardia Airport reported 3.6 inches of snow. A Cocorahs observer reported 2.8 inches at 0.3 SE Little Neck and a trained spotter reported 2.0 inches in Little Neck, with the public reported 2.7 inches at 2 ENE Fresh Meadows and 2.7 inches at 1 SE Fresh Meadows. The zone was right at the cusp of advisory level criteria.

An Official NWS Observation of 2.2 inches was reported at JFK Airport. A Cocorahs observer reported 3.8 inches at Howard Beach and the public reported 3.8 inches at Bellerose just to the north. Most locations reported just below advisory level criteria, especially further south, while locations at the northern edge of the zone are estimated to be right around advisory level criteria.
The public reported 3.5 inches at 1 E New Dorp and 2.6 inches in Westerleigh.  Snowfall was right at the cusp of advisory level criteria.

Broadcast media reported 2.7 inches at Midwood and a trained spotter reported 2.5 inches at Sheepshead Bay. The public reported 3.0 at Bedford-Stuyvesant, 3.0 inches at 1 NNE Sheepshead Bay and 2.2 inches at 1 N Bay Ridge.  Amounts generally averaged just below advisory criteria for the zone.

Trained spotters reported 3.0 inches in Hoboken, 3.0 inches in Kearney, with the pubic reporting 3.1 inches in West New York and 2.5 inches in Jersey City. A Cooperative observer reported 3.0 inches in Harrison.  Amounts averaged around the bottom end of advisory level criteria.

Cocorahs reported 6.2 inches in West Milford. A trained spotter reported 5.6 inches at Pompton Lakes, with the pubic reporting 6.3 inches in Ringwood.  Amounts were close enough to warning level criteria to verify the warning for this zone.

Cocorahs observers reported 5.6 inches in Little Falls, 4.8 inches in Wayne, 4.2 inches in Hawthorne. The public reported 5.0 inches in Totowa and 4.8 inches in Passaic.  Snow amounts on average reached advisory level criteria.

Trained spotters reported 5.9 inches in Franklin Lakes and 3.4 inches at 1 WSW Wallington. The public reported 4.5 inches in Oakland. Cocorahs reported 5.0 inches in Fair Lawn.  Advisory level snow was reached in the zone.

Trained spotters reported 5.2 inches in Westwood, 5.0 inches in River Vale, 4.8 inches in Bergenfield, and 3.3 inches at East Rutherford. Cocorahs reported 5.5 inches at 1.8 ESE Montvale. The public reported 3.2 inches at River Edge.  Advisory level snow was reached across the zone.
Cocorahs reported 5.0 inches in Montclair and 3.1 inches in Maplewood. The public reported 4.4 inches in Livingston and 5.0 inches in Caldwell.  Advisory level snow was reached across the zone.

The public at 1 SSW West Orange reported 4.5 inches. Just to the east and southeast many reports at around 3 inches were reported.  Maplewood received 3.1 inches and Elizabeth reported 3.7 inches from a trained spotter, and Newark Airport receiving 2.4 inches. The eastern portion of Essex and thus the zone was estimated to have reached advisory criteria.

The public reported 5.1 inches in Scotch Plains, 4.5 inches in Berkeley Heights, and 4.5 inches in Mountainside. A trained spotter reported 3.5 inches in Plainfield. A cocorahs observer reported 4.5 inches in New Providence. Advisory level snow criteria was reached across the zone.

A trained spotter reported 3.5 inches in Cranford. A cocorahs observer reported 3.0 inches at 1.1 ESE Cranford and 2.8 inches at Clark. A trained spotter reported 3.7 inches in Elizabeth, with the Official NWS observation at Newark Airport at 2.4 inches.  The zone averaged out at the low end of advisory level criteria.

Trained spotters reported 3.0 inches in Islip and 3.0 inches in North Babylon. Cocorahs observers reported 1.6 inches in Bay Shore and 1.5 inches at 0.5 W Islip Terrace.  Amounts averaged below advisory level criteria across the zone with only the northern edge of the zone right at 3 inches.

The Meriden ASOS reported 0.54 inches of ice, Broadcast media at Hamden reported 0.25 inches of ice, and a trained spotter reported 0.25 inches of ice at North Haven. Tree branches and wires were reported down in Hamden, with large branches reported down in West Haven. Route 243 was closed between Baldwin  Road and Wepawaug Road because of wires down.   Generally 1 to 2 inches of snow fell before the changeover to freezing rain across the zone.  Trained spotters reported 2.0 inches at 1 NNW North Haven and at 1 ENE North Haven, 2.0 inches at Meriden, and 1.8 inches 2 NW Waterbury. Utility company (Eversource) reported at least 15,400 customers were without power, with nearly 1,500 of those located in Newtown, with nearly 1,200 United Illuminating customers as of 24 hours after the storm. By 42 hours after the storm on the following Monday morning Eversource upped the number to 85,000.

Power outages were reported among utility companies. The utility company reported / estimated 0.30 inches of ice at 3 W Higganum with power outages reported. Everclear utility reported thousand of power outages in the Higganum area. Power lines were reported down off Route 154 in Haddam. And based on radar a large swath of the northern half of Northern Middlesex would have experienced around a half inch of ice. 1 to 3 inches of snow fell before the changeover to freezing rain. Due to impacts and radar estimation of QPF while temperatures were at or below freezing, winter storm / ice warning criteria is estimated to have been reached. Trained spotters reported 2.8 at 4 W Cromwell, 2.3 inches at Higganum, 2.0 inches at Middletown, and 1.5 inches in Durham.

Snow of approximately 1 to 2.5 inches fell in the late afternoon and evening before the changeover to freezing rain.  ASOS reported 0.48 inches of ice at Danbury Airport, and trained spotters reported 0.35 inches in New Fairfield, 0.40 inches at 4 NNW New Fairfield, and 0.25 inches in Newtown. Several downed trees and wires were reported in Newtown and lots of tree limbs were reported down around North Street at 2 N Ridgefield, and a tree across Taylor Road in Bethel which took down wires, all via the public.  Large branches and medium sized limbs reported breaking and a limb took down a power line resting on a truck. Scattered power outages were reported across the zone.

The Montgomery ASOS reported 0.52 inches of ice and a trained spotter reported 0.31 inches of ice in Monroe. With radar estimates while temperatures were below freezing along with impacts, warning criteria was estimated to be reached across the northern half of the zone. 1 to 2 inches of snow fell across the central and northern portions of the zone before the change to freezing rain. Large branches were reported down in Chester with some scattered outages across north central Orange County.

With respect to snow, 1 to 2 inches in all likelihood was reached around the county / zone before the change to freezing rain. Poughkeepsie ASOS just to the north reported just a half inch of ice, and there were reports to the west and east of or near a half inch of ice which included Danbury ASOS.  Based on radar estimates in and around Putnam county warning criteria with respect to ice is estimated to have been reached.

An estimated 1 to 2 inches of snow with some sleet fell across a good portion of Northern Westchester, especially further north across the zone, before a changeover to freezing rain.  A trained spotter reported 1.4 inches of snow in Peekskill just before midnight and before the changeover. A tree fell on a house in North Salem from a public report. Also a tree down with wires was reported by the Department of Highways resulting in a road closure in both directions on NY Route 121 between Bloomer Road and Vail Lane.

Mainly 3 to 4 inches fell across the zone with the majority of the accumulating snow falling during the late evening hours. Generally 3 to 4 inches were reported across the zone. Trained spotters reported 4.1 inches in Washingtonville, 3.8 inches at 1 WNW Monroe, and 3.0 inches at 2 SSW Harriman.  Cocorahs observers reported 3.9 inches at Cornwall on the Hudson, 3.8 inches at 4 SSE Chester, and 3.1 inches at Warwick.

Mainly 3 to 5 inches fell across the zone. Trained spotters reported 4.0 inches at Croton-on-Hudson and 4.0 inches in Peekskill. The public reported 3.5 inches in Ossining. Cocorahs observers reported 4.0 inches in Armonk and 3.8 inches in South Salem.

An accumulating snowfall of mainly 3 to 5 inches fell across the zone. Trained spotters reported 3.2 inches at 2 NW Woodlawn, 4.0 inches at 2 NNE White Plains, and 4.5 inches at 1 ESE Hartsdale. The public reported 4.8 inches at 1 N Eastchester, 4.8 inches in Mamaroneck, and 4.6 inches at 1 SSE Port Chester.
Mainly 3 to 4 inches fell across the zone, with not a lot of snowfall reports for the zone. Cocorahs reported 3.5 inches at 0.3 S Nelsonville, and 3.0 inches in Cold Spring.

An accumulating snowfall of mainly 3 to 4 inches occurred across the county / zone. Cocorahs observers reported 3.9 inches in Stony Point and 3.2 inches at 1.7 SSW Spring  Valley. A trained spotter reported 3.5 inches in New City.
The general public reported 4.6 inches at 1 ENE Fordham and 3.1 inches at 1 NW Fordham.

Most reports were in the 3 to 4 inch range across the zone. The public reported 4.1 inches at Whitestone and 3.1 inches at Bellerose, with 3.6 inches at LaGuardia airport. Cocorahs reported 3.2 inches at 0.3 SE Little Neck.
Most snowfall reports were in the 3 to 4 inch range. Cocorahs reported 3.7 inches at Howard Beach, while JFK airport reported 3.4 inches.
Central Park Conservancy reported 3.1 inches, with a public report of 1.5 inches at 1 SSW Greenwich Village the following morning likely following some compaction.
Trained spotters reported 3.0 inches at both 1 WNW Crown Heights and Sheepshead Bay. Broadcast media reported 2.8 inches at Midwood.
The public reported 2.2 inches at Dongan Hills.

Generally 3 to 5 inches of snow fell across the zone, with some light freezing rain and drizzle overnight after the snow tapered off. Cocorahs observers measured 4.3 inches at 1.4 SSE Hicksville and 3.9 inches in Herricks. The Public reported 3.9 inches at Manhasset Hills, 3.8 inches in Sea Cliff, and 3.8 inches in Westbury.

Generally 3 to 4 inches of snow fell across the zone with a change to light freezing rain and drizzle during the overnight after the burst of snow on the front end. Trained spotters reported 3.2 inches at 1 SE Malverne and 2.8 inches in Merrick.  Cocorahs observers reported 3.2 inches in Massapequa Park and 3.0 inches in Bellmore.

Mainly 4 to 5 inches of snow fell across the zone, with a changeover to light freezing rain and drizzle towards and after midnight for a portion of the overnight, followed by another round of lighter snow early in the morning. Trained spotters reported 5.0 inches in Smithtown, 4.3 inches in Hauppauge. NWS Employees reported 4.5 inches at 1 N Setauket-East Setauket, 4.5 inches in Centereach, and 4.4 inches in Stony Brook. Islip Airport reported 0.10 inches of freezing rain.

Generally 3 to 4 inches fell across the zone with a changeover to freezing rain and drizzle after the front end thump of accumulating snow. Islip Airport reported 4.0 inches of snow along with 0.10 inches of freezing rain. Cocorahs observers reported 3.3 inches at both 1.0 SSE Bayport, 0.5 W Islip Terrace, Babylon, along with 3.0 inches in Amityville.

Generally 4 to 5 inches fell across the zone before a change to light freezing rain and drizzle overnight. Cocorahs reported 5.0 inches at 1.5 SE Ridge, 4.3 inches in Ridge, and 4.5 inches at Port Jefferson Station. The public reported 4.2 inches in Miller Place, and COOP observers reported 5.0 inches at Orient Point and 4.0 inches in Baiting Hollow. An official NWS observation of 4.6 inches was reported in Upton. A trained spotter reported 4.8 inches in Mattituck.

Generally 3 to 4 inches of snow fell across the zone before the snow mixed and changed to mixed precipitation and light rain and drizzle during the overnight before briefly ending as some light snow early in the morning. NWS employees reported 3.4 inches in Patchogue and 3.6 inches in East Quogue. The public reported 4.8 inches in Hampton Bays and 4.5 inches in Yaphank.

Accumulating snow fell across the zone mostly in a 4 to 5 hour period, mainly during the late evening across the zone, with brief mixed precip and lighter snow afterwards towards early morning. Cocorahs observers reported 6.1 inches in Sandy Hook, 5.0 inches at 5.3 S Newtown, 4.7 inches in Bethel, and 4.8 inches in Ridgefield. Trained spotters reported 5.0 inches at 1 E Danbury and at 5 ENE Redding, along with 4.2 inches at 4 NNW New Fairfield. Danbury ASOS reported 0.02 inches of freezing rain.

Average snowfall totals were around 4 inches across the zone. Trained spotters reported 3.8 inches at 2 SSW Weston, 4.2 inches at Weston, and 4.5 inches in Wilton. The official NWS observation at Bridgeport was 5.0 inches. Cocorahs reported 5.0 inches in New Caanan, 4.9 inches at 2.6 SSE Trumbull, 4.4 inches at 1.0 S Stamford, and 4.0 inches at Stratford.

Generally 4 to 5 inches of snow fell across the zone from the mid to late evening and into the early portions of the overnight as far as accumulation goes. Trained spotters reported 5.2 inches in Hamden, 5.0 inches in Seymour, and 3.3 inches in Waterbury. Cocorahs reported 4.0 inches at 2.3 W Southbury and 3.5 inches in Meriden.

Accumulating snow fell during the second half of the evening and into a portion of the overnight. The snow did mix with and change to freezing rain for a time. Trained spotters reported 3.7 inches at 1 SW Branford and 4.0 inches at 1 ENE North Haven, and 5.0 inches in North Haven.

There were multiple reports of downed trees or limbs in the area, including a NWS Employee reporting a large downed tree branch on Montauk Highway in Remsenburg-Speonk at 1005 AM Local Standard Time, and a trained spotter reporting a large tree down on Montauk Highway in Bridgehampton at  1035 AM Local Standard Time.

A mesonet station in Syosset recorded at 62 mph high wind gust at 924 AM Local Standard Time. At 642 PM Local Standard Time, a high wind speed gust of 58 mph was recorded at mesonet station Robbins Reef Lighthouse in Bayonne, NJ, at an elevation of 69 feet above ground.
Fire Department/Rescue reported a person struck by a tree at 612 PM Local Standard Time along Route 303 in Blauvelt with the person having chest and shoulder pain.
Local Fire Department/Rescue reported live wires down on a car in Yonkers at 502 PM Local Standard Time.
At 642 PM Local Standard Time, a high wind speed gust of 58 mph was recorded at mesonet station Robbins Reef Lighthouse in Bayonne, NJ, at an elevation of 69 feet above ground.
Fire Department/Rescue reported live wires down on Ridge Drive in Berkeley Heights at 537 PM Local Standard Time.

A couple of high wind gusts were recorded by mesonet stations. Additionally, a gust of 60 mph was recorded by a station in Fairfield at 1055 AM Local Standard Time.

A couple of high wind gusts were recorded by mesonet stations. This included a gust of 65 mph at station XHAM - Hammonasset in Madison at 1023 AM Local Standard Time. Additionally, a gust of 58 mph was recorded by a station in Stony Creek at 1041 AM Local Standard Time.
A high wind gust was recorded by Mesonet station CT002 Middletown - Rt9nb in Middletown at 1029 AM Local Standard Time.

A car was stranded in high waters under a flooded viaduct at East Main St. and Crescent Ave. in Bridgeport.  The 2 occupants (an adult and a child) were rescued by local firefighters. A new school on Waterview Ave. in Bridgeport was also flooded.

A school bus became stuck in high waters (up to the bumper) at the intersection of Creek Rd. and New York Ave. in Halesite. At least 4 children were rescued by the local fire department.

Numerous trees and power lines were reported down throughout Westport.

A microburst occurred in Harrington Park along a west to east running path one-quarter mile long and 200 yards wide. This path was roughly from 21 Harriot Avenue, where it appears the microburst made first contact with the ground, to the western border of the town. The microburst brought down multiple large tree branches, and a few large trees, causing damage to 5 to 10 houses and some parked cars, including a 2008 limited edition Mustang Bullitt. Based on the damage, peak winds from this microburst were estimated at around 90 mph.  In addition, multiple trees were downed in Old Tappan near where the Hackensack River goes through the town.

Deep water covered Loring Road, which caused flooding in Levittown.

Flooding caused a one story building to partially collapse with people trapped in it at 3rd Ave. and East 182nd St. in East Tremont.  Local media reported that there were no injuries, but the fire department determined that the remaining portion of the structure was too unstable and had to be demolished.
All lanes on the Bronx River Pkwy. northbound at E. 233rd St. in East Tremont were closed due to flooding.
The Saw Mill River Pkwy. was closed between exits 25 and 27 in Hawthorne due to flooding.
There were many flooded highways and road closures in Port Richmond.
The Belt Parkway in Bensonhurst was closed due to flooding.
Sparkill Creek overflowed its banks flooding several streets in Tappan. A bridge on Oak Tree Road, also in Tappan, was inundated with water and closed to traffic.
The Hutchinson River Pkwy. was closed between Cross County Pkwy. and the New York City line due to flooding.
Numerous roads were closed in Jersey City due to flooding.
Six inches of moving water was reported on Linwood Ave. in Ridgewood.
Frank E. Rodgers Blvd. near Middlesex St. and Cape May St. in Harrison was closed due to flooding.
Newark Turnpike was closed from the New Jersey Tpke. to Route 7 in Kearny due to flooding.
Three feet of water inundated Route 440 at Danforth Ave. in Jersey City and was closed.

Heavy rain caused major flooding of a newly constructed tanning salon in Ramsey.  There was basement flooding and the building inspector and rescue squad were called in due to concerns of a structural collapse from leaks in the foundation.
Meeker Ave. at Elizabeth Ave. in Newark was closed with cars floating due to flooding.
Valley Road in Wayne was inundated with water and impassable.
Numerous roads were under water and closed in Garwood.

Elmora Ave. at Fay Ave. in Elizabeth was closed due to flooding with water rescues being performed. A car rescue due to flood waters was also performed at the intersection of 3rd Ave. and S. 2nd St. also in Elizabeth.
Water rescues were performed on Cortland Street in Belleville.

There was major flooding along Route 17 closing much of it as well as Route 3 in both directions in Rutherford and East Rutherford. Route 17 was also closed due to flooding between Route 46 and Polify Rd. in Hasbrouck Heights. Route 46 (eastbound) was closed at Summit Ave. in Hackensack and also in Lodi due to flooding. Three people were rescued from their car after they became trapped by flood waters in Bogota.
McCarter Highway in Newark was closed due to flooding. Routes 1 and 9 (southbound) were also closed in Newark with cars stalled in flood waters.
Two feet of water was reported on portions of Sound Beach Ave. and Arcadia Rd. in Greenwich.

Many roads in Danbury were under 1-2 ft. of water. One to three feet of standing water was reported on the roads in and near the campus of Western Connecticut State University on White Street. A one hour rainfall rate of 1.43 inches was reported between 6 pm and 7 pm in Danbury.
Route 2 in North Stonington was closed due to flooding.
River Trail in Southbury was closed due to flooding.
Flooding rains caused a road collapse on Lemoine Ave. in Fort Lee.
I-278 (Brooklyn-Queens Expressway) was closed in both directions at Broadway due to flooding.

Four people had to be rescued from their SUV at the intersection of New York Ave. and Creek Rd. in Halesite after it became stranded in 4 ft. of standing water.  The intersection was then closed off to traffic.
The westbound Route 59 ramp to southbound Route 303 in West Nyack was closed due to flooding.
The southbound Hutchinson River Pkwy. was closed at East Lincoln Ave. in Mount Vernon due to flooding.
The Sprain Brook Pkwy (southbound) was closed where it merges with the Bronx River Pkwy. in Mount Vernon due to flooding.
The Taconic State Pkwy. was closed in both directions at Stevens Ave. in Mount Pleasant due to flooding.
The Belt Pkwy. eastbound exit ramp to Flatbush Ave. was closed due to flooding.
The Bronx River Pkwy. (northbound) was closed at 236th St. due to flooding.
Warburton Ave. near Arthur St. in Yonkers was closed due to flooding.
Portions of Bell Blvd. in Bayside were flooded.
In Woodside, 66th Street and 48th Ave. were inundated with water, which flooded some adjoining residential properties.

In Paterson, Hwy 19 was closed in both directions at Valley Rd. and Rt. 20 (southbound) was closed at Broadway due to flooding. Around 30 cars were partially submerged in the Best Buy and Kohl's parking lot off of Route 46 in West Paterson. Emergency personnel had to evacuate stranded shoppers in the Little Falls Civic Center on Warren St. in Little Falls. Overflowing storm drains turned roads into moats around the Third Ward Park on Passaic Ave. and Glenside Ave. in Passaic.  Finally, flooding submerged Riverside Dr. near the Home Depot and other low-lying sections of the borough.

North Benson Road in Fairfield was closed due to flooding. Iranistan Ave. in the area of State St., Fairfield Ave., and Railroad Ave. were inundated with flood waters. About 25 areas in Bridgeport were flooded and 10 water rescues were performed by local emergency personnel.

A homeless man was swept down the Norwalk River from his home under the Cross Street Bridge.  His body was found at 8:15 am Sunday morning off of Chimon Island, just outside Norwalk Harbor. The medical examiner determined the death was consistent with drowning with a boat propeller injury occurring after death.

The Ho-Ho-Kus River at Ho-Ho-Kus exceeded its flood stage of 3.0 ft. at 6:15 pm local time. The river crested at 3.98 ft. at 10 pm and fell below flood stage on 9/7/08 at 2:45 am. The Saddle River at Lodi exceeded its flood stage of 6.0 ft. at 6:15 pm local time. The river exceeded moderate flood stage at 11:45 pm and crested at 7.77 ft. on 9/7/08 at 4:15 am. The river fell below flood stage on 9/7/08 at 8 am.

The Third River at Bloomfield exceeded its flood stage of 6.0 ft. at 8:15 pm local time. The river crested at 7.37 ft. at 9:15 pm and fell below flood stage on 9/7/08 at 12:15 am. The Peckman River at Verona exceeded its flood stage of 3.5 ft. at 8:45 pm local time. The river crested at 4.10 ft. at 10:15 pm and fell below flood stage at 11 pm.

The Rahway River at Springfield exceeded its flood stage of 5.5 ft. at 7 pm local time. The river crested at 7.29 ft. at 9:45 pm and fell below flood stage on 9/7/08 at 3:15 am. The Elizabeth River at Ursino Lake exceeded its flood stage of 20.0 ft. at 7:30 pm local time. The river crested at 20.73 ft. at 8:45 pm and fell below flood stage at 11 pm.
Molly Ann Brook at N. Haledon exceeded its flood stage of 6.0 ft. at 7:05 pm local time. The river crested at 6.65 ft. at 7:15 pm and fell below flood stage 9:15 pm.
The Pomperaug River at Southbury exceeded its flood stage of 9.0 ft. on 9/7/08 at 3:15 am local time. The river crested at 9.17 ft. at 5:45 am and fell below flood stage at 7:15 am.

In Springfield Gardens, 147th Ave. was closed due to flooding. Water levels were approximately 6 inches deep on 147th St. in Rosedale, where  local authorities taped off the road. Flood waters also caused raw sewage to back up into some homes in Rosedale.
Route 218 was closed in both directions in Cornwall due to flooding.
Flash flooding occurred on Route 17 at Midland Ave. in Paramus and in the Highland Cross area of Rutherford. The Dept. of Transportation had to pump water off the road in both locations.

The NOS tidal gauge at Kings Point reported moderate coastal flooding from 10:32 am EDT to 12:14 pm EDT. The peak surge was 2.5 feet, which was obtained by subtracting the observed tide from the predicted tide at the NOS gauge.
The weather station at Cardinal Hayes High School measured a wind gust to 51 mph at 6:39 pm EDT.
A wind gust to 55 mph was measured at the West New York weather station at 5:28 pm EDT.  Numerous trees and wires were downed at 238 York Avenue in Jersey City at 4:49 pm EDT.

A wind gust to 53 mph was measured by the Fort Lee weather station at 4:38 pm EDT.  High winds downed numerous trees and power lines in Fort Lee.  Power lines were downed at 23 Daniel Court in Ridgewood.  Trees and wires were downed on 66 East Crescent Avenue in Ramsey.
The general public reported a wind gust of 52 mph in Clinton at 8:44 pm EDT.  High winds downed trees near the intersection of Routes 3 and 372 in Cromwell.
A fifty foot silver maple tree cracked at its base and fell on a man walking along the sidewalk on South Center Street, in Orange.

Major flooding was realized in the towns of Yantic, Greeneville, Norwichtown, and parts of East Great Plain from the Yantic River reaching moderate and then cresting at major flood stage.  Many businesses experienced flooding and were forced to close while they pumped water out of their storefronts. Several roads, such as West Town Street in Yantic Flats, were also closed. Total rainfall amounts ranged from 3.25 inches to 4.5 inches in New London County. The Yantic River at Yantic exceeded its flood stage of 9.0 ft. at 6:30 am on Dec 12th.  The river exceeded moderate flood stage of 9.5 ft. at 7:15 am and major flood stage of 11.5 ft. at 10:30 am before cresting at 11.82 ft. at 11:45 am.  The river remained above flood stage through the day and finally receded back within its banks at 11:45 pm on Dec 12th.
Flooding forced the closure of both ends of Pickett Lane, blocking access to Coginchaug High School and Korn School from both Maiden Lane and Main Street in Durham.
Route 9 was closed in Essex Village due to flooding.

The combination of heavy rain and the Pequonnock River exceeding bankfull caused flooding and the closing of Water Street in Bridgeport. Total rainfall at Sikorsky Airport in Bridgeport was 3.73 inches.

Campbell Avenue was closed in West Haven due to major flooding.  Total rainfall at New Haven/Tweed Airport was 3.93 inches.  The Quinnipiac River at Wallingford and the Pomperaug River at Southbury both rose to minor flooding levels.  The Quinnipiac River at Wallingford crested at 10.81 ft. (flood stage is 10.0 ft.) and the Pomperaug River at Southbury crested at 9.85 ft. (flood stage is 9.0 ft.).
Montauk Highway was closed in Shinnecock Hills due to major flooding.
The Southern State Pkwy. was closed at the Cross Island Pkwy. due to extensive roadway flooding.

The Saddle River at Lodi exceeded its flood stage of 6.0 ft at 5 am.  The river crested at 6.36 ft. at 9 am, but Route 46 was closed upstream of the gage due to flooding. Total rainfall amounts in Bergen County ranged from 2.75 inches to 3.85 inches.
The Rahway River at Springfield exceeded its flood stage of 5.5 ft. at 12:15 am and crested at 6.36 ft. at 5:45 am. This led to flooding and eventual closing of Route 22 in Springfield.
Springfield Ave. was closed in Irvington due to flooding.
Union Valley Road was closed in West Milford due to flooding.

A severe thunderstorm that produced storm damage in Bergen county in|northeastern New Jersey moved into Yonkers around 11:25 pm as the|storm intensified.  Doppler weather radar analysis would classify|the storm as a supercell with a strong mesocyclone at this time. A|large area of very strong downburst winds downed numerous large|trees that fell on structures, power lines and cars. The worst damage|observed in the area was in Trevor Park around the Hudson River|Museum where winds were estimated to have gusted up to 100 mph. Some minor damage appeared to occur to the roof of the Museum with a few shingles blown off. Nearly all trees appeared to have fallen to the east or southeast. The damage area extended east to North Broadway and into Grant Park on Park Ave where numerous large trees were also knocked over falling to the east or southeast. Downed large trees were also observed in Oakland Cemetery.||Downed trees were also observed in Mount Vernon along West Street|and Macquesten Parkway North where winds of 70 mph were estimated to|have occurred. Again, all trees appeared to fall to the southeast.|There was additional tree damage to a lesser degree to the north|observed along and near the Cross County Parkway.||In Bronxville, several trees were seen downed along the Bronx River|Parkway from exits 1 to 3. In Eastchester and Tuckahoe, several large|trees were downed in the vicinity of Ridge and Governors Roads. A|large tree here fell on power lines snapping a telephone pole in|half. Winds in this area were estimated at 80 mph.||In addition to the wind damage, there was extensive hail from the|storm along with torrential rain. The hail accumulated to several|inches in Yonkers and was still visible this morning. Rain swept the|hail into some locations to depth over a foot. In one location on|Hoover Road in northern Yonkers...up to 4 feet of hail accumulated|inside a home after the drainage became clogged.

Also at this time in Freeport, a few feet of water was reported over Hudson Street, and several streets along the Nautical Mile were under water and impassable.|At 9:00 am (EDT) a maximum water level of 8.96 feet MLLW was reported at the USGS gauge at Inwood, this is 0.26 feet above the bench mark for moderate tidal flooding.|At 11:50 am (EDT) overwash flooding was reported on Bayville Avenue in Bayview.|At 12:00 pm (EDT) a maximum water level of 10.51 feet MLLW was reported at the NOS gauge at Kings Point, this is 0.01 feet above the bench mark for moderate tidal flooding.

Strong winds downed trees and tree limbs onto wires and cars.  Power failures were reported in the Huguenot and Huguenot Beach sections.  A tree fell on the Staten Island Railway's St. George-bound train track near Grasmere station around 1:40 pm EDT.
